figures.finding: Vanuatu levies no personal income tax: no tax falls on an individual's pay or fees (a 15% tax on rental income over VT 200,000 in six months is the only income levy, and it does not touch screen work).

sources.said: With no taxes affecting individuals other than import duties (at varying rates), there is effectively no corporate and personal income tax in vanuatu
No Income Taxes Vanuatu offers NO Income Tax

figures.finding: With no income tax there is no individual tax year or return.

sources.said: With no taxes affecting individuals other than import duties (at varying rates), there is effectively no corporate and personal income tax in vanuatu

figures.finding: The Vanuatu National Provident Fund takes 8% of an employee's monthly remuneration, 4% from the employee and 4% from the employer, with no ceiling stated; expatriate employees contribute too unless approved to pay into an overseas fund; the self-employed (a freelancer) need not join but may as voluntary members.

sources.said: Currently, the rate of contribution is 8% of the employee's remuneration, of which 4% is from the employee's monthly remuneration while 4% is contributed by the employer.

Expatriate employees are also subject to Vanuatu law and must make contributions, unless they have been approved by VNPF to have their contributions directed to an alternative overseas superannuation fund
Self-employed workers, including employers, are not obliged to join, however they can join and contribute as a Voluntary Member

figures.finding: No income tax is withheld from pay or fees; only the employee's 4% provident fund contribution is deducted.
A non-resident performer, writer or director pays no Vanuatu income tax and has nothing withheld from a fee.

figures.finding: With no income tax, authors' fees and royalties are untaxed.

figures.finding: VAT is 15% on most supplies by a registered person in a taxable activity; registration is required once taxable supplies in any 12 months exceed, or are expected to exceed, VT 4 million, and is voluntary below.
figures.applies: A freelancer carrying on a taxable activity

sources.said: VAT is an indirect consumption tax imposed at the rate of 15% on most goods and services supplied in Vanuatu by registered persons in the course of a taxable activity.

A person must be registered for VAT if they carry on a taxable activity and their total taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceeds, or is expected to exceed, VT4 million. Persons with an annual turnover of less than VT 4 million have the option of registering for VAT
